author: BBC News
description:
US President Donald Trump has issued an expletive filled threat against Iran if the Strait of Hormuz is not re-opened to shipping.  

He is threatening to destroy Iran’s infrastructure, including power stations and bridges, acts that human rights organisations are warning would amount to war crimes.  Trump reiterated his previous threat to unleash “hell” on Iran if it did not meet his deadline. 

Earlier, he announced that a US airman missing in Iran, after his F-15 fighter jet was shot down, had been rescued in a daring military operation.   The pilot had already been rescued by US forces.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Joe Inwood and Orla Guerin.

The US President has threatened to target civilian infrastructure inside Iran, if a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is not reached with Tehran.

The very strongly worded social media post followed new details of a daring US mission to rescue a second US airman, stranded for around 48-hours inside Iran after a US fighter jet was shot down.

As rhetoric around the Strait of Hormuz escalates, our Senior International Correspondent reports from the Gulf of Oman on what a potential US operation there could look like.

author: BBC News
description:
US President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden threat against Iran's infrastructure if the Strait of Hormuz is not opened.

Trump said "Tuesday will be Power Plant Day, and Bridge Day, all wrapped up in one" in Iran if the key shipping lane is not reopened.
 
He reiterated his earlier threat to unleash "hell" if the country does not meet his 6 April deadline, though previous deadlines given by the president have shifted.
 
The Strait of Hormuz is a key trade artery through which around 20% of the world's oil passes and since the beginning of the US-Israeli war with Iran, numerous ships have come under attack in the area.

author: BBC News
description:
The crew for Nasa's Artemis II mission are now over halfway on their journey to the Moon.
 
Astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen have entered the third day of their mission on the Orion spacecraft, and have now caught their first glimpse of the far side of the Moon.
 
The crew shared a photo they took of the Orientale basin of the Moon, which Nasa said marked "the first time the entire basin has been seen with human eyes".
 
As of 23:00 BST on Saturday, Nasa's online dashboard showed the Artemis II spacecraft was more than 180,000 miles (289,681km) from Earth.

author: BBC News
description:
An American crew member rescued after a fighter jet was shot down over Iran is “safe and sound”, US President Donald Trump said.
 
The operation to rescue the airman led to an engagement between US and Iranian forces, after a race to locate them, with Iranian officials offering cash rewards to citizens to find them "alive”.
 
It is understood the rescue was a hugely complex operation involving significant US military resources, with hundreds of special forces personnel, several dozen warplanes and helicopters tasked with the search.
